conclusion.cross_round_result: Byte shuffle commutes with XOR after transforming the constant, but not with the intervening modular ADD; two round-boundary shuffles cannot be cancelled.
conclusion.qualification: The UNSAT result is grammar-scoped, and LLVM-MCA is only a scheduling proxy rather than a Core Ultra 7 255H measurement.
conclusion.result: No three-instruction BSWAP64-plus-rotate network exists in the scoped AVX2 shift/shuffle/bitwise grammar. The three constructive split-shuffle controls are exact but add one VPSHUFB per round, increasing the measured loop from 122 to 142 instructions.

identity_and_pair_boundary_checks.cross_round_conclusion: XOR commutes with BSWAP after swapping the constant, but modular addition does not. The intervening first-round ADD therefore blocks cancellation of the two round-boundary byte shuffles.

grammar.byte_shuffle: each output byte may independently choose any byte of the same 64-bit word or zero; this is a word-local superset of the selections useful to exact lane-preserving VPSHUFB
grammar.combine: XOR or OR; carry-free ADD is identical to OR/XOR on disjoint bit fields and is therefore covered
grammar.exhaustively_enumerated_program_shape: two independent unary instructions from the input followed by XOR/OR; identity is admitted as a zero-count shift
grammar.qword_shift: logical left/right by any independently chosen lane count 0..63, granting more freedom than one shared immediate

other_three_instruction_dag_shapes.coverage: Together with the exhaustively enumerated parallel branch shape, these are all topological placements of zero, one, or two binary operations in a three-operation single-input DAG.
other_three_instruction_dag_shapes.one_unary_and_two_binary_combines: At each bit these DAGs compute one fixed two-input Boolean function of the raw bit and the unary-produced bit. To equal a bit permutation for every input, that function must reduce globally to one projection; the result is therefore identity or the sole unary, neither of which is the target.
other_three_instruction_dag_shapes.three_serial_unaries: A nonzero logical shift in a one-register unary chain leaves fewer than 64 distinct live source bits. A chain containing only byte shuffles preserves source/destination bit positions modulo eight. Neither can implement this 64-bit permutation with a non-byte rotate.
other_three_instruction_dag_shapes.two_serial_unaries_then_combine_with_raw: If the first unary is lossy, neither descendant branch can recover all 64 source bits. If it is bijective, it is an identity shift or byte permutation. Factoring that bijection leaves identity combined with one unary; XOR/OR can equal a one-bit projection at every output only when that projection is the identity. The whole DAG then collapses to the first one-instruction transform, for which the exhaustive solution count above is zero.
other_three_instruction_dag_shapes.unary_after_one_unary_plus_raw_combine: The last unary must be bijective, because the target uses all 64 source bits exactly once. Pulling back through it again leaves identity combined with one unary, which can only be the identity projection; the last unary would then have to be the target, contradicted by the zero one-instruction solution count.

three_instruction_linear_network.scope_limit: This is a lower bound only for AVX2 networks built from qword logical shifts, arbitrary fixed byte selections, and XOR/OR or carry-free ADD. It is not a lower bound over every x86 opcode.

acquisition.method: download the pinned llvm-19 and libllvm19 .deb files, extract them under any directory, and pass the resulting llvm-mca and library-directory paths through --llvm19-mca and --llvm19-lib-dir; runtime files remain content-addressed

scheduler_source_evidence.interpretation: LLVM 19 exposes the Arrow Lake CPU name but assigns it the AlderlakePModel scheduler. It is not an exact 255H model.

reused_harness.scope: container build, official/random verifier, loop parser, and LLVM-MCA plumbing only; candidate generation and shape contracts are defined by this driver

model_limits.llvm_mca: LLVM-MCA 16 Alder/Meteor/Zen 2 and LLVM-MCA 19 Arrow Lake/Arrow Lake-S/Lunar Lake/Sierra Forest models are public scheduling proxies. None is asserted to be an exact Core Ultra 7 255H P/E/LP-E model, and none models frequency effects.
model_limits.synthesis: This is a lower bound only for AVX2 networks built from qword logical shifts, arbitrary fixed byte selections, and XOR/OR or carry-free ADD. It is not a lower bound over every x86 opcode.
model_limits.target_timing: No host result can promote a candidate; exact 255H confirmation remains a separate hardware task.
